note: A TEMP DIRECTORY IS NOT ISOLATION WHEN THE ENVIRONMENT NAMES THE REPOSITORY. If you run a git-touching test suite from a hook in a LINKED WORKTREE, it can write to the real repo even though every call passes -C tempdir. Measured today at real cost. Mechanism: git -C sets the working DIRECTORY but does not scope which REPOSITORY git acts on, because GIT_DIR outranks it, and git exports an ABSOLUTE GIT_DIR plus GIT_INDEX_FILE to every hook it runs from a linked worktree. So every git -C tempdir in the suite operated on the developer checkout and the temp dirs never became repositories at all. One fact explains all of it: git init re-initialised the real repo and guessed BARE, because a worktree gitdir does not end in slash dot git, so the primary checkout stopped being a work tree; git config rewrote user.name to the test identity, so every later commit in the repo was mislabelled; test helpers landed commits and branches on main; and a test write planted a ref pointing at a nonexistent object, which broke git fetch repository-wide. Note the primary checkout is BENIGN, it gets no GIT_DIR and a relative index, so this only bites from a worktree, which is how all campaign work commits. Fix: scrub GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, GIT_NAMESPACE, the GIT_AUTHOR and GIT_COMMITTER sets, and GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS, before you add -C. Also env minus u on any hook line that runs the suite. Inspecting your own helper will NOT find this: ours passed -C correctly and used a unique temp dir, and both were right individually, because the leak lives in the environment which neither function reads.
